<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8d242457431d817d58b445fbe0e63cc2f1f17cd` — the merge of head `656657595b803b3c9ee684e5ece3b8a42addc4f9` into base `b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8d242457431d817d58b445fbe0e63cc2f1f17cd && git checkout d8d242457431d817d58b445fbe0e63cc2f1f17cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745 656657595b803b3c9ee684e5ece3b8a42addc4f9 && git checkout -B drift-repro b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745 && git merge --no-ff 656657595b803b3c9ee684e5ece3b8a42addc4f9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b0ef25f524b870433424b8ad797ef3801374f745` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `656657595b803b3c9ee684e5ece3b8a42addc4f9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/action-confirm-params-guard.test.ts, .changeset/29383-inline-action-confirm-beside-params-refused.md, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, content/docs/references/kernel/metadata-plugin.mdx, content/docs/references/ui/action.mdx, content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-component-props.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx, ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, AGENTS.md

Inputs read: card #29383 body and all nine comments (triage 6580249013, claim 6580616231, measurement report 6580676225, decision card 6580700185, hand-off 6589420791, ruling 6595808462 letter A, seat claims 6595853086 and 6595887076, os-dev-report 6597115604); PR #29829 body, its seven-file list, and the net diff of `65665759` against merge base `b3d14150` with `origin/main` (19 commits ahead); the 42 check-runs on `65665759`; and the cited code at that head: `action.zod.ts` (`actionObject`, `declaresConfirmBesideParams`, `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL`, `ActionSchema`, `normalizeInlineAction`, `InlineActionSchema`), the guard test with its `base` / `oneParam` / `guardIssue` helpers, `component.zod.ts` (`ElementButtonPropsSchema.action`, `ActionButtonPropsSchema`, `ComponentPropsMap`), `page.zod.ts:662` (the component `properties` record) and its door comment at 2264, `validate-component-props.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts:176,471-476,1285-1312`, `compile.ts:541,577`, `elements.tsx:345-420`, `ActionRunner.ts:1650-1740,2011`, the ADR-0087 checker (its `CATEGORIES`, `findMigrationPrescription`, the `no-migration-prescription` fact check), the level checker's level-axis docblock, ADR-0087's marker grammar, AGENTS.md § Touched `packages/spec`, Prime Directive #14 and rule 3 of the finishing list, and the two precedent changesets `26413-now-anchor-extra-key-refused.md` and `26462-diff-missing-version-refused.md` on `origin/main`. The face: `--paths` on the seven files returns `hits` = `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (a published schema); the PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the narrowing face applies and the tier is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER either way.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept-set change the diff implies is exactly one refusal, on one door.** `InlineActionSchema` gains one `.refine(...)` whose predicate is the negation of `declaresConfirmBesideParams(data)` and whose issue is `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL`, between its target-required rule and the url-target `superRefine`. The predicate is: `confirmText` is neither `null` nor `undefined`, and `params` is an array of length at least one; byte for byte the condition `ActionSchema` carried inline on `main`; the refusal object is the `ActionSchema` message moved to module level, unchanged, with `path: ['confirmText']`. `ActionSchema`'s refinement now reads `return !declaresConfirmBesideParams(data)` with the same object. One predicate, one message, two doors: right, and the test pins the two messages equal with `toBe`.
2. **Nothing else in the accept set moves.** No key is added to or removed from the pick; `normalizeInlineAction` (the preprocess) rewrites only `navigation` to `url` and `to` to `target`, so it cannot manufacture or hide a `confirmText` / `params` pair before the refine. `confirmText` alone, `confirmText` beside `params: []`, and `description` beside `params` all still parse (three accept controls in the test). The locale-map form of `confirmText` is refused beside `params` because the predicate reads `!= null`, which is the registered door's reading too. `BulkActionDefSchema` is untouched and its accept pin stays in the renamed boundary block. Right.
3. **The describe change is true on every door that renders it.** The `confirmText` describe on the shared field factory drops "On a registered action,". That describe renders on `ActionSchema` (object actions in `data/object.mdx`, `kernel/metadata-plugin.mdx`, `ui/action.mdx`) and on `InlineActionSchema` (`ui/action.mdx` second table, and the `ElementButtonProps.action` nested table in `ui/component.mdx` at L237, which I located under the `## ElementButtonProps` heading; the hunk's `ActionButtonPropsSchema.parse` context line is git's heuristic, not the table). Both doors now refuse the pair, so the unqualified sentence is true at every render site. `action:button`'s own `confirmText` uses `ACTION_ROW_COPY_DESCRIBE.confirmText`, a different describe, and is not touched. Right.
4. **The four regenerated reference pages carry only that phrase.** I diffed the five removed table rows against the five added rows after substituting "On a registered action, pairing this" with "Pairing this": identical. No other describe or type moved in the regen, which matches the PR's claim that `check:generated` found only `check:docs` stale. Right.
5. **The measurement that grounds the ruling holds in the cited code.** `elements.tsx` forwards `confirmText` as is and an array `params` as `actionParams` to `execute(...)` from `useAction()`; `ActionRunner.execute` computes `confirmMessage(action)` (returns text whenever `confirmText` is declared, with no `params` branch) and awaits `confirmHandler` before it reads `actionParams` and awaits `paramCollectionHandler`. Two dialogs, in that order, for an inline action, exactly as 6580676225 read it. Right.
6. **The refinement comment moves from "not decided here" to the ruling.** The `ActionSchema` comment now names #29383 and record 6595808462 letter A, and the inline refine carries the same reference. Right.
7. **Test shape.** The old inline acceptance pin ("out of reach too") is removed from the boundary block and the block is renamed to say what it still pins (the bulk def keeps the pair); a new five-test block pins the refusal (path, `code: 'custom'`, message equal to `ActionSchema`'s and containing "TWO dialogs" and "`description`"), the locale-map refusal, and the three accept controls. The helpers it uses (`base`, `oneParam`, `guardIssue`) are defined at the file head. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29383-inline-action-confirm-beside-params-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed (...)`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one `adr-0087:` marker. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. The only package the diff moves is `@objectstack/spec` (the lint, cli and ui files I read are cited, not changed). Under the level checker's level axis (`narrowed` ⇒ at least one moved package `minor`+; the `(narrowing)` arm is the breaking signal and ships `minor` during the launch window), `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is the level the rule prescribes, and the cross-checks that would contradict (`narrowed` without a `(narrowing)` arm; `added` under `no`) are not tripped. The Check Changeset run on the head (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base`) concluded `success`. Level and declarations match the diff.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind: "a value refused ... a requirement tightened" is the AGENTS.md definition, and an author may no longer write `confirmText` beside a non-empty `params` on a page button's inline action.
- No `skip-changeset`, no `major`, no second package. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev flag: the ADR-0087 disposition as a marker, no `docs/adr/**` path.** Judged against AGENTS.md rule 3 ("A breaking changeset must also state its ADR-0087 disposition, in writing — exactly one marker in the changeset body"), ADR-0087's marker grammar (`not-required (no-migration-prescription) why` is one of the seven published forms), the checker's `CATEGORIES` (it is a member), and the checker's fact check for this category (refused only when the body carries a migration prescription; the Check Changeset run passed, so the detector found none in "The remedy" paragraph). The ruling 6595808462 asks for "an ADR-0087 disposition"; the earlier hand-off's word "entry" is the dev report's guess, and the ruling is what binds. The closest precedent, `26413-now-anchor-extra-key-refused.md` on `main`, is a spec `minor` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and the same `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and it touched no `docs/adr/**` path. A `docs/adr/**` edit would also be a Tier H governed-surface edit (Prime Directive #14) that this Tier S PR could not land on its own. With census 0 shipped carriers, no key added, removed or renamed, and a remedy that needs the author to read the sentence, this is the repo's accepted disposition for the case. Answered: holds.
2. **Dev finding: `defineStack` does not judge the pair; the door is lint `validateComponentProps`.** The page component's `properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`page.zod.ts:662`), so the stack parse never dispatches a component's props to `ComponentPropsMap`; `page.zod.ts:2264` says in its own words that the bag is judged by `@objectstack/lint`'s `validateComponentProps` at the CLI doors and the runtime save door. The rule's registration in `authoring-rules.ts` is `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL` (`validate`, `build`, `lint`), `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME` (`cli`, `runtime-publish`), `runtimeTypes: ['page']`, and the gate dispatches `element:button` to `ElementButtonPropsSchema`, whose `action` is `InlineActionSchema.optional()`. `os compile` runs `runAuthoringRules('build', ...)` (`compile.ts:577`), so it is the `build` command the gate names. The claimed door is real on every command and on the runtime `page` write; the changeset's "a stored page keeps loading; its next save is refused" matches the registration comment ("the gate judges writes, never the read path"). Other doors: `defineStack` / `definePage` accept the pair silently, by design of the open bag, for every props defect and not this one; a stored page row is not replayed. Boundary flag, not a must-fix, and the changeset already names it. Answered.
3. **Sibling door observation, outside the ruling.** `ActionButtonPropsSchema` (`action:button`, a different component) carries its own `confirmText` and a `params: z.unknown()` whose array form the renderers forward to the same runner as `actionParams` (the ui tests under `renderers/action/__tests__` say so); it carries no pair rule, so an `action:button` with `confirmText` beside an array `params` opens the same two dialogs and is accepted. Ruling A binds `InlineActionSchema` only, the PR claims nothing about `action:button`, and widening the refusal to a third door is a separate narrowing decision. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card, not a finding on this PR.
4. **Deviation: 19 commits behind `main`, not merged.** Of the 19, two touch a PR file: `138dacf6ce` (a `relatedList` describe) and `eeb3117a5e` (object extension field keys) regenerate `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` at L254, L577 and L625; the PR's hunk is at L495. Neither touches `action.zod.ts`, the guard test, the changeset, or the other three reference pages. The merge queue rebuilds on `main`, `check:docs` reruns there, and the hunks are disjoint, so the deviation does not bear on landing. The dev's reason (keeping the dogfood reading pinned to the reviewed head) is sound. Answered: no action.
5. **`open_questions` on 6597115604:** none. The report's two `out_of_scope_findings` (the hand-written `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` L444 and `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` L22, both still true but naming only the registered door) are outside the claim surface; the skills line is a Tier H edit. Both stay true sentences, so leaving them is correct for this PR; the seat may file a docs follow-up. Answered.
6. **Check-runs on `65665759` at review time:** 42 runs. Concluded `success`: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, filter. `skipped`: 18.x harness, Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. Still `in_progress` with no conclusion: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1-8, Type Check · consumer gates, debt ledger, source gates, workspace. The `check:docs` / `check:api-surface` / `check:authorable-surface` verdicts therefore sit in a Type Check run not yet concluded; the queue guard reads them before landing. Reported as seen, not waited for. The PR body's local readings (spec 804 files / 23884 tests, lint consumers 207 tests, dogfood 3326 tests, 102 derived gates) are the dev's account and are not adopted here.
7. **Governed surfaces:** none of the seven paths is under `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/workflows/**`. The Governed Surface Queue Guard concluded `success`. Tier S landing on this record.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` — holds.** Judged against the ruling it implements (6595808462 letter A), the published spec on `main`, and its first consumers (`ElementButtonPropsSchema.action` through lint `validateComponentProps`; the `element:button` renderer through `ActionRunner`).

- *Does it make the spec's own refusal real at the consumer?* Yes. The ruling binds "the same predicate and message family `ActionSchema` uses ... Issue path `confirmText`"; the diff uses the same function and the same object, so the two doors cannot drift apart in wording, and the test pins the messages equal. The refusal reaches the author at `pages[N].regions[N].components[N].properties.action.confirmText` through the gating rule at every CLI command and the runtime `page` write.
- *Does it take a declared capability away beyond the ruling?* No. The only pair refused is `confirmText` beside a non-empty `params` array; `params` on the inline pick is the `ActionParam[]` definition only, so `Array.isArray` is the complete reading, and `params: []`, no `params`, and the `description` remedy all parse. The remedy slot exists on the inline pick (`description: true`, since #29369), and the message names it.
- *Attempts to break it.* (a) The preprocess cannot reshape the pair (it only renames `navigation` / `to`). (b) Refine order: zod 4 runs every `.refine` on the chain unless `abort` is set, so the url-target `superRefine` still reports on the same body; the test reads the issue by path, not by index. (c) A blank `confirmText` (`''`) is `!= null` and refused beside params on both doors alike, consistent with `main`. (d) The locale-map arm is refused, as on `ActionSchema`. (e) `BulkActionDefSchema` is a separate `strictObject` with its own refinements; nothing in this diff can reach it, and its pin stays green by construction. (f) No export is added or removed (`declaresConfirmBesideParams` and `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL` are module-private), so `check:api-surface` has nothing to move; no key is added, so `check:authorable-surface` has nothing to move.
- *Must-fix:* none.
- *Should-fix:* none on the hits file. For the seat's follow-up list only (not this PR): the `action:button` sibling in ③.3, and the two hand-written prose sites in ③.5.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:行内动作(`InlineActionSchema`,页面按钮的 `properties.action`)同时写 `confirmText` 和非空 `params` 时拒收,判定和报错文字与注册动作(`ActionSchema`)完全同一份;只写 `confirmText`、或配 `params: []`、或把问句放进 `description`,都照常通过。
- 为什么改:执行 #29383 裁决 A(记录 6595808462):这对组合在控制台会先弹确认框、再弹参数框,两个对话框问同一件事;注册动作早已拒收,行内动作是漏网的那扇门。
- 风险与回滚:一处收窄(`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`),仓库内已发元数据里带这对组合的行内动作为 0,只翻转了 spec 自己的一条测试 pin;作者在 `os validate` 和运行时页面保存时看到拒收与改法。回滚即撤回本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` 的 `declaresConfirmBesideParams` 与 `InlineActionSchema` 的新 refine,再看 `action-confirm-params-guard.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/ui/action-confirm-params-guard.test.ts`,两扇门的拒收文字相同,三个通过对照全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

席位意见:同一谓词、同一文案、两扇门,契约复审在收窄档 PASS,全量 dogfood 在本 head 0 失败;同意落地。复审另看到 `action:button` 的 `ActionButtonPropsSchema` 也能带这对组合且无拒收,属裁决 A 之外的新问题,已转到裁决讨论线程由你定。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `656657595b803b3c9ee684e5ece3b8a42addc4f9`
